subject: math
title: Length Word Problems and Number Lines
seo_title: Grade 2 Length Word Problems Worksheets: Number Lines, Adding and Subtracting Lengths within 100
standard_text: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem. Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 length word problem worksheets: numbers as lengths on a number line, adding and subtracting with jumps, joining, cutting and comparing lengths, missing lengths with ☐ equations and two-step stories. 100 practice questions with simple answers.
key_big: A length is the number of spaces from the start to the end.
key_sub: On a number line, jump right to add and left to subtract. In a story, draw the lengths, write an equation with a ☐ and keep the same unit: 60 cm − 25 cm = 35 cm.
body_html:
A number is a length from 0

On a number line, the marks are equally spaced. Each space is 1 unit, like 1 centimeter or 1 inch. The number 7 is 7 spaces from 0. So a length is the number of spaces, not the number of marks.

Add and subtract with jumps

To add, start at the first number and jump right. To subtract, jump left. Big jumps of 10 first, then small jumps, make it easy.

Draw the story, then write an equation

Draw the lengths as bars. Put a ☐ where the unknown number goes. All the lengths in one story use the same unit.

Take away

A rope is 60 centimeters long. Ava cuts off 25 centimeters. How long is the rope now?

Part is taken away, so subtract: 60 − 25 = ☐. 60 − 20 = 40, then 40 − 5 = 35.

Answer: 35 centimeters

Compare

A tree is 32 feet tall. A fence is 6 feet tall. How much taller is the tree than the fence?

Find the difference: 32 − 6 = ☐. Count up from 6 to 32: that is 26.

Answer: 26 feet

Missing start

A ribbon was some inches long. Leo cut off 18 inches. Now it is 46 inches long. How long was it at first?

☐ − 18 = 46. Put the cut piece back: 46 + 18 = 64.

Answer: 64 inches

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the marks: the crayon is 8 cmCount the spaces between the marks: 7 cm
Reading the end of a length that does not start at 0Subtract the start from the end: 9 − 4 = 5
Counting the start number as the first jumpStart at 45, then count 46, 47, … The first step lands on 46.
Adding when the question asks “how much longer”Compare means find the difference: subtract
Writing the wrong unitUse the unit in the story: feet stay feet

faq.q: What are length word problems in 2nd grade?
faq.a: They are add and subtract stories about lengths, like ribbons, ropes, plants and paths, with numbers up to 100. All the lengths in one problem use the same unit, such as centimeters or feet.

faq.q: Why do 2nd graders use a number line for length?
faq.a: A number line works like a ruler: each number is a length from 0. Children see adding as a jump to the right and subtracting as a jump to the left.

faq.q: Why do children get the wrong length on a number line or ruler?
faq.a: They count the marks instead of the spaces, so they get 1 too many. A length is the number of spaces from the start to the end.

faq.q: Do 2nd graders convert units in word problems?
faq.a: No. In 2nd grade every length in a problem uses the same unit. Converting units, like feet to inches, comes in 4th grade.

sets.title: Numbers as lengths on a number line

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 30. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37. 30 + 7 = 37. (It is also 3 before 40.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 70. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 71, 72, 73, 74. 70 + 4 = 74. (It is also 6 before 80.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 20. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28. 20 + 8 = 28. (It is also 2 before 30.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 40. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46. 40 + 6 = 46. (It is also 4 before 50.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 80. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 81, 82, 83. 80 + 3 = 83. (It is also 2 before 85.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 30. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 31, 32. 30 + 2 = 32. (It is also 3 before 35.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 10. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 11, 12, 13. 10 + 3 = 13. (It is also 2 before 15.)

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 9. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 9 spaces. Each space is 1 centimeter, so it is 9 centimeters long.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the caterpillar?
items.e: The caterpillar starts at 0 and ends at 5. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 5 spaces. Each space is 1 centimeter, so it is 5 centimeters long.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the leaf?
items.e: The leaf starts at 0 and ends at 8. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 8 spaces. Each space is 1 centimeter, so it is 8 centimeters long.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the ribbon?
items.e: The ribbon starts at 0 and ends at 13. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 13 spaces. Each space is 1 centimeter, so it is 13 centimeters long.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 7. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 7 spaces. Each space is 1 inch, so it is 7 inches long.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the craft stick?
items.e: The craft stick starts at 0 and ends at 6. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 6 spaces. Each space is 1 inch, so it is 6 inches long.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the paper strip?
items.e: The paper strip starts at 0 and ends at 9. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 9 spaces. Each space is 1 inch, so it is 9 inches long.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the eraser?
items.e: The eraser does not start at 0. It goes from 4 to 9. Subtract: 9 − 4 = 5. Or count the spaces from 4 to 9: 5. Answer: 5 centimeters.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the nail?
items.e: The nail does not start at 0. It goes from 3 to 10. Subtract: 10 − 3 = 7. Or count the spaces from 3 to 10: 7. Answer: 7 centimeters.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the paper strip?
items.e: The paper strip does not start at 0. It goes from 5 to 14. Subtract: 14 − 5 = 9. Or count the spaces from 5 to 14: 9. Answer: 9 centimeters.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil does not start at 0. It goes from 2 to 15. Subtract: 15 − 2 = 13. Or count the spaces from 2 to 15: 13. Answer: 13 centimeters.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the ribbon?
items.e: The ribbon does not start at 0. It goes from 3 to 8. Subtract: 8 − 3 = 5. Or count the spaces from 3 to 8: 5. Answer: 5 inches.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon does not start at 0. It goes from 2 to 6. Subtract: 6 − 2 = 4. Or count the spaces from 2 to 6: 4. Answer: 4 inches.

items.q: Start at 45. Jump 20 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 45 and move 20 spaces: 45 + 20 = ☐. 45 + 20 = 65.

items.q: Start at 23. Jump 30 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 23 and move 30 spaces: 23 + 30 = ☐. 23 + 30 = 53.

items.q: Start at 58. Jump 14 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 58 and move 14 spaces: 58 + 14 = ☐. 58 + 10 = 68. Then 68 + 4 = 72.

items.q: Start at 36. Jump 25 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 36 and move 25 spaces: 36 + 25 = ☐. 36 + 20 = 56. Then 56 + 5 = 61.

items.q: Start at 17. Jump 18 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 17 and move 18 spaces: 17 + 18 = ☐. 17 + 10 = 27. Then 27 + 8 = 35.

items.q: Start at 64. Jump 27 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 64 and move 27 spaces: 64 + 27 = ☐. 64 + 20 = 84. Then 84 + 7 = 91.

items.q: Start at 72. Jump 30 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 72 and move back 30 spaces: 72 − 30 = ☐. 72 − 30 = 42.

items.q: Start at 55. Jump 16 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 55 and move back 16 spaces: 55 − 16 = ☐. 55 − 10 = 45. Then 45 − 6 = 39.

items.q: Start at 81. Jump 25 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 81 and move back 25 spaces: 81 − 25 = ☐. 81 − 20 = 61. Then 61 − 5 = 56.

items.q: Start at 46. Jump 19 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 46 and move back 19 spaces: 46 − 19 = ☐. 46 − 10 = 36. Then 36 − 9 = 27.

items.q: Start at 90. Jump 37 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 90 and move back 37 spaces: 90 − 37 = ☐. 90 − 30 = 60. Then 60 − 7 = 53.

items.q: How long is the jump from 34 to 52?
items.e: Count up from 34 to 52, or subtract: 52 − 34 = 18. Check: 34 + 18 = 52. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 48 to 75?
items.e: Count up from 48 to 75, or subtract: 75 − 48 = 27. Check: 48 + 27 = 75. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 26 to 41?
items.e: Count up from 26 to 41, or subtract: 41 − 26 = 15. Check: 26 + 15 = 41. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 57 to 83?
items.e: Count up from 57 to 83, or subtract: 83 − 57 = 26. Check: 57 + 26 = 83. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: The jumps are +20 and +5. Together they make 25. Start at 30 and add 25: 30 + 25 = 55.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: The jumps are +20 and +8. Together they make 28. Start at 43 and add 28: 43 + 28 = 71.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: Both jumps go left, so subtract. −20 and −6 make −26: 74 − 26 = 48.

items.q: Which number line shows 30 + 25?
items.e: Number line B starts at 30 and jumps 25 to the right, to 55. 30 + 25 = 55.

items.q: Which number line shows 62 − 24?
items.e: Number line C starts at 62 and jumps 24 to the left, to 38. 62 − 24 = 38.

sets.title: Join lengths: put them end to end

items.q: Dad puts two boards end to end. One board is 45 inches long. The other board is 34 inches long. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 45 + 34 = ☐. 45 + 34 = 79, so the total is 79 inches.

items.q: A bean plant was 17 centimeters tall. It grew 25 centimeters this month. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 17 + 25 = ☐. 17 + 25 = 42, so the total is 42 centimeters.

items.q: A bookshelf is 29 inches long. Ben puts a second bookshelf 27 inches long next to it, end to end. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 29 + 27 = ☐. 29 + 27 = 56, so the total is 56 inches.

items.q: Kai rides his bike 46 meters to a friend's house. Then he rides 44 meters to school. How far does Kai ride in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 46 + 44 = ☐. 46 + 40 = 86. Then 86 + 4 = 90. (6 + 4 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 90 meters.

items.q: Jack has a red ribbon 27 centimeters long and a blue ribbon 32 centimeters long. He tapes them end to end. How long is the new ribbon?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 27 + 32 = ☐. 27 + 30 = 57. Then 57 + 2 = 59. Answer: 59 centimeters.

items.q: A garden fence has two parts. One part is 39 feet long. The other part is 25 feet long. How long is the whole fence?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 39 + 25 = ☐. 39 + 20 = 59. Then 59 + 5 = 64. (9 + 5 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 64 feet.

items.q: The class paints a red line 18 meters long on the playground. Then they paint a blue line 36 meters long at the end of it. How long are the two lines together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 18 + 36 = ☐. 18 + 30 = 48. Then 48 + 6 = 54. (8 + 6 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 54 meters.

items.q: Ms. Park hangs two banners end to end. One banner is 9 feet long. The other is 12 feet long. How long are the two banners together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 9 + 12 = ☐. 9 + 10 = 19. Then 19 + 2 = 21. (9 + 2 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 21 feet.

items.q: Emma built a block tower 35 centimeters tall. Then she added blocks to make it 21 centimeters taller. How tall is the tower now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 35 + 21 = ☐. 35 + 20 = 55. Then 55 + 1 = 56. Answer: 56 centimeters.

items.q: Mia lays a pencil and a crayon end to end. The pencil is 17 centimeters long. The crayon is 9 centimeters long. How long are they together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 17 + 9 = ☐. 17 + 9 = 26. (7 + 9 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 26 centimeters.

items.q: Owen walks 33 meters to the corner. Then he walks 28 meters to the park. How far does he walk in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 33 + 28 = ☐. 33 + 20 = 53. Then 53 + 8 = 61. (3 + 8 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 61 meters.

items.q: A sunflower was 49 inches tall. Then it grew 18 more inches. How tall is the sunflower now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 49 + 18 = ☐. 49 + 10 = 59. Then 59 + 8 = 67. (9 + 8 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 67 inches.

items.q: A worm crawled 13 centimeters. Then it crawled 14 centimeters more. How far did the worm crawl in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 13 + 14 = ☐. 13 + 10 = 23. Then 23 + 4 = 27. Answer: 27 centimeters.

items.q: A paper chain is 19 feet long. The class makes 13 more feet of chain. How long is the chain now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 19 + 13 = ☐. 19 + 10 = 29. Then 29 + 3 = 32. (9 + 3 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 32 feet.

items.q: Zoe swam 38 meters. Then she swam 37 more meters. How far did Zoe swim in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 38 + 37 = ☐. 38 + 30 = 68. Then 68 + 7 = 75. (8 + 7 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 75 meters.

items.q: Maya knit a scarf 24 inches long. Then she knit 18 more inches. How long is the scarf now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 24 + 18 = ☐. 24 + 10 = 34. Then 34 + 8 = 42. (4 + 8 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 42 inches.

items.q: Two rugs lie end to end in a hallway. One rug is 13 feet long. The other rug is 12 feet long. How long are the two rugs together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 13 + 12 = ☐. 13 + 10 = 23. Then 23 + 2 = 25. Answer: 25 feet.

items.q: A toy train has three cars. The cars are 16 centimeters, 17 centimeters and 14 centimeters long. How long is the train?
items.e: Add all three lengths: 16 + 17 + 14 = ☐. First 16 + 17 = 33. Then 33 + 14 = 47. Answer: 47 centimeters.

items.q: A trail has three parts. They are 16 meters, 21 meters and 18 meters long. How long is the whole trail?
items.e: Add all three lengths: 16 + 21 + 18 = ☐. First 16 + 21 = 37. Then 37 + 18 = 55. Answer: 55 meters.

items.q: Lily tapes three paper strips end to end. They are 18 inches, 17 inches and 11 inches long. How long is the long strip?
items.e: Add all three lengths: 18 + 17 + 11 = ☐. First 18 + 17 = 35. Then 35 + 11 = 46. Answer: 46 inches.

items.q: Omar has to walk 88 meters to the library. He has walked 45 meters so far. How much farther does he have to walk?
items.e: You know the whole way and the part already walked. Subtract to find the part still to go: 88 − 45 = ☐. 88 − 40 = 48. Then 48 − 5 = 43. Check: 43 + 45 = 88. Answer: 43 meters.

items.q: A roll of paper is 55 feet long. Noah cuts off 17 feet for a class poster. How long is the roll now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 55 − 17 = ☐. 55 − 10 = 45. Then 45 − 7 = 38. Check: 38 + 17 = 55. Answer: 38 feet.

items.q: A roll of tape had 60 feet of tape. The class used 19 feet. How many feet of tape are left?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 60 − 19 = ☐. 60 − 10 = 50. Then 50 − 9 = 41. Check: 41 + 19 = 60. Answer: 41 feet.

items.q: A candle was 28 centimeters tall. It burned down 9 centimeters. How tall is the candle now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 28 − 9 = ☐. 28 − 9 = 19. Check: 19 + 9 = 28. Answer: 19 centimeters.

items.q: A garden hose is 65 feet long. A piece 23 feet long is cut off. How long is the hose now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 65 − 23 = ☐. 65 − 20 = 45. Then 45 − 3 = 42. Check: 42 + 23 = 65. Answer: 42 feet.

items.q: A board is 95 inches long. Dad saws off 39 inches. How long is the board now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 95 − 39 = ☐. 95 − 30 = 65. Then 65 − 9 = 56. Check: 56 + 39 = 95. Answer: 56 inches.

items.q: A race is 80 meters long. Leo has run 22 meters. How many more meters does he need to run?
items.e: You know the whole race and the part already run. Subtract to find the part still to run: 80 − 22 = ☐. 80 − 20 = 60. Then 60 − 2 = 58. Check: 58 + 22 = 80. Answer: 58 meters.

items.q: A ribbon is 41 inches long. Luis cuts off 14 inches to make a bow. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 41 − 14 = ☐. 41 − 10 = 31. Then 31 − 4 = 27. Check: 27 + 14 = 41. Answer: 27 inches.

items.q: A rope is 78 centimeters long. Emma cuts off 24 centimeters. How long is the rope now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 78 − 24 = ☐. 78 − 20 = 58. Then 58 − 4 = 54. Check: 54 + 24 = 78. Answer: 54 centimeters.

items.q: A string is 72 centimeters long. Mia uses 43 centimeters to make a necklace. How much string is left?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 72 − 43 = ☐. 72 − 40 = 32. Then 32 − 3 = 29. Check: 29 + 43 = 72. Answer: 29 centimeters.

items.q: A tree is 29 feet tall. A fence is 7 feet tall. How much taller is the tree than the fence?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 29 − 7 = ☐. 29 − 7 = 22. Check: 7 + 22 = 29. Answer: 22 feet.

items.q: A sunflower is 76 inches tall. A tulip is 22 inches tall. How much shorter is the tulip than the sunflower?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 76 − 22 = ☐. 76 − 20 = 56. Then 56 − 2 = 54. Check: 22 + 54 = 76. Answer: 54 inches. “How much shorter” is the same difference.

items.q: The big pool is 25 meters long. The small pool is 8 meters long. How much shorter is the small pool?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 25 − 8 = ☐. 25 − 8 = 17. Check: 8 + 17 = 25. Answer: 17 meters. “How much shorter” is the same difference.

items.q: Grace is 51 inches tall. Ruby is 43 inches tall. How much taller is Grace than Ruby?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 51 − 43 = ☐. 51 − 40 = 11. Then 11 − 3 = 8. Check: 43 + 8 = 51. Answer: 8 inches.

items.q: A blue ribbon is 49 centimeters long. A red ribbon is 27 centimeters shorter than the blue ribbon. How long is the red ribbon?
items.e: The red ribbon is shorter, so subtract: 49 − 27 = ☐. 49 − 20 = 29. Then 29 − 7 = 22. Answer: 22 centimeters.

items.q: Omar's paper airplane flew 24 feet. Noah's plane flew 17 feet farther. How far did Noah's plane fly?
items.e: Noah's plane flew farther, so add: 24 + 17 = ☐. 24 + 10 = 34. Then 34 + 7 = 41. Answer: 41 feet.

items.q: A school bus is 41 feet long. It is 25 feet longer than a van. How long is the van?
items.e: The word “longer” is in the story, but the van is the shorter one, so subtract: 41 − 25 = ☐. 41 − 20 = 21. Then 21 − 5 = 16. Answer: 16 feet.

items.q: A green toy snake is 63 centimeters long. A red toy snake is 47 centimeters long. How much longer is the green snake?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 63 − 47 = ☐. 63 − 40 = 23. Then 23 − 7 = 16. Check: 47 + 16 = 63. Answer: 16 centimeters.

items.q: A desk is 29 inches tall. It is 34 inches shorter than a bookshelf. How tall is the bookshelf?
items.e: The word “shorter” is in the story, but the bookshelf is the taller one, so add: 29 + 34 = ☐. 29 + 30 = 59. Then 59 + 4 = 63. Answer: 63 inches.

items.q: Emma jumped 51 inches. Mia jumped 42 inches. How much farther did Emma jump than Mia?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 51 − 42 = ☐. 51 − 40 = 11. Then 11 − 2 = 9. Check: 42 + 9 = 51. Answer: 9 inches.

items.q: A ribbon was some inches long. Owen cut off 18 inches. Now the ribbon is 46 inches long. How long was it at first?
items.e: The start is unknown: ☐ − 18 = 46. Put the cut piece back: 46 + 18 = 64. Answer: 64 inches.

items.q: A plant grew 16 centimeters this month. Now it is 53 centimeters tall. How tall was it at the start of the month?
items.e: The start is unknown: ☐ + 16 = 53. Take away what it grew: 53 − 16 = 37. Answer: 37 centimeters.

items.q: A bean plant was 28 centimeters tall. It grew some more. Now it is 45 centimeters tall. How many centimeters did it grow?
items.e: The change is unknown: 28 + ☐ = 45. Count up from 28 to 45 on the number line, or subtract: 45 − 28 = 17. Answer: 17 centimeters.

items.q: A paper chain was 36 feet long. The class made it longer. Now it is 62 feet long. How many feet did they add?
items.e: The change is unknown: 36 + ☐ = 62. Count up from 36 to 62 on the number line, or subtract: 62 − 36 = 26. Answer: 26 feet.

items.q: A rope was 80 centimeters long. Sofia cut some off. Now it is 53 centimeters long. How much did she cut off?
items.e: The change is unknown: 80 − ☐ = 53. Think: 53 + ☐ = 80. Subtract: 80 − 53 = 27. Answer: 27 centimeters.

items.q: Nora has to walk 95 meters to the park. She has 68 meters left to go. How far has she walked so far?
items.e: The change is unknown: 95 − ☐ = 68. Think: 68 + ☐ = 95. Subtract: 95 − 68 = 27. Answer: 27 meters.

items.q: A rope was some feet long. Zoe cut off 19 feet. Now it is 46 feet long. Which equation can you use to find how long it was at first?
items.e: The start is unknown, and 19 feet were cut off: ☐ − 19 = 46. Answer: 46 + 19 = 65 feet.

items.q: A tower was 34 centimeters tall. Maya added some blocks. Now it is 61 centimeters tall. Which equation can you use to find how much taller it got?
items.e: The tower got taller by an unknown amount: 34 + ☐ = 61. Answer: 61 − 34 = 27 centimeters.

items.q: A ribbon was 72 inches long. Grace cut off some. Now it is 45 inches long. Which equation can you use to find how much was cut off?
items.e: An unknown length was cut off: 72 − ☐ = 45. Answer: 72 − 45 = 27 inches.

items.q: A sunflower grew 17 inches. Now it is 58 inches tall. Which equation can you use to find how tall it was before?
items.e: The start is unknown, and it grew 17 inches: ☐ + 17 = 58. Answer: 58 − 17 = 41 inches.

items.q: A board is 90 inches long. Sam saws off 25 inches. Then he saws off 32 more inches. How long is the board now?
items.e: Step 1: First cut: 90 − 25 = 65. Step 2: Second cut: 65 − 32 = 33. Equation: 90 − 25 − 32 = ☐. Answer: 33 inches.

items.q: Lily's block tower is 36 centimeters tall. Omar's tower is 15 centimeters taller. Omar puts his tower on top of Lily's tower. How tall is the new tower?
items.e: Step 1: Omar's tower: 36 + 15 = 51. Step 2: Together: 36 + 51 = 87. Equation: 36 + 36 + 15 = ☐. Answer: 87 centimeters.

items.q: A path is 80 meters long. The class walked 26 meters. Then they walked 35 more meters. How much farther is it to the end of the path?
items.e: Step 1: Walked: 26 + 35 = 61. Step 2: Still to go: 80 − 61 = 19. Equation: 80 − 26 − 35 = ☐. Answer: 19 meters.

items.q: Noah has a red ribbon 34 centimeters long. His blue ribbon is 18 centimeters longer. He tapes them end to end. How long is the new ribbon?
items.e: Step 1: Blue ribbon: 34 + 18 = 52. Step 2: Both: 34 + 52 = 86. Equation: 34 + 34 + 18 = ☐. Answer: 86 centimeters.

items.q: A fence will be 60 feet long. Workers built 23 feet on Monday and 19 feet on Tuesday. How many more feet do they need to build?
items.e: Step 1: Built: 23 + 19 = 42. Step 2: Still to build: 60 − 42 = 18. Equation: 60 − 23 − 19 = ☐. Answer: 18 feet.

items.q: A sunflower was 25 inches tall. It grew 12 inches in June and 16 inches in July. How tall is it now?
items.e: Step 1: June: 25 + 12 = 37. Step 2: July: 37 + 16 = 53. Equation: 25 + 12 + 16 = ☐. Answer: 53 inches.

items.q: A rope is 75 centimeters long. Ben cuts off a piece 24 centimeters long and a piece 18 centimeters long. How much rope is left?
items.e: Step 1: Cut off: 24 + 18 = 42. Step 2: Left: 75 − 42 = 33. Equation: 75 − 24 − 18 = ☐. Answer: 33 centimeters.

items.q: Kai is 47 inches tall. He stands on a box that is 15 inches tall. A door is 84 inches tall. How much taller is the door than Kai on the box?
items.e: Step 1: Kai on the box: 47 + 15 = 62. Step 2: Difference: 84 − 62 = 22. Equation: 84 − 47 − 15 = ☐. Answer: 22 inches.

items.q: A race is 100 meters long. Jack ran 45 meters. Then he walked 28 meters. How much farther does he have to go?
items.e: Step 1: So far: 45 + 28 = 73. Step 2: Still to go: 100 − 73 = 27. Equation: 100 − 45 − 28 = ☐. Answer: 27 meters.

items.q: Ava jumped 38 inches. Leo jumped 9 inches farther than Ava. Luis's jump was 6 inches shorter than Leo's. How far did Luis jump?
items.e: Step 1: Leo: 38 + 9 = 47. Step 2: Luis: 47 − 6 = 41. Equation: 38 + 9 − 6 = ☐. Answer: 41 inches.
